title: The Best Players Never to Play in the Premier League—Ranked
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Barnaby LaneNov 24, 2026Messi and Alves were a dream team. / Alex Caparros/Getty ImagesSince its inception in 1992, the Premier League has been home to some of the greatest soccer players of the modern era.

From Eric Cantona’s enigmatic brilliance and Thierry Henry’s elegance to Kevin De Bruyne’s midfield mastery and Eden Hazard’s dazzling footwork, England’s top flight has never been short of extraordinary talent.

That said, not every world-class player has graced the Premier League stage. Plenty of superstar names have spent their entire careers elsewhere, choosing to remain in mainland Europe or venture even further afield rather than test themselves on English soil.
Here, we’ve ranked the 30 greatest players never to play in the Premier League.

Ribery was some player. / Lars Baron/Bongarts/Getty ImagesIt took Franck Ribéry a while to establish himself on soccer’s biggest stage, but his 2007 move to Bayern Munich was where his career truly took off.The electric Frenchman remained in Bavaria until 2019, collecting trophies as if they were nothing and tormenting defenders on the wing along the way. Sheffield United reportedly made him an offer in 2019, but he opted to join Fiorentina instead.

Bellingham would thrive in the Prem. / Mateo Villalba/Getty ImagesLike a few other current stars on this list, Jude Bellingham still has time to make his mark in the Premier League.His imposing frame and experience in the Championship with Birmingham City would make him an ideal fit if he ever returned to English soccer.

Dani Alves was immense for Barca. / Manuel Queimadelos/Quality Sport Images/Getty ImagesThe first of several Brazilian fullbacks on this list, Dani Alves was a key member of the legendary Barcelona squad that won it all under Pep Guardiola.His partnership with Lionel Messi on the right flank was particularly devastating—a combination he likely would have replicated with someone else had he ever made the move to the Premier League.

Kaka almost joined Man City. / Claudio Villa/Getty ImagesHad Manchester City got their way in 2009, Kaká would have arrived in the Premier League midway through the season, giving fans a chance to marvel at his brilliance while tormenting Manchester United and Liverpool on a more regular basis.It wasn’t meant to be, though. He joined Real Madrid that summer instead.

Marcelo was world class. / David Ramos/Getty ImagesPerhaps one of the sport’s most underrated players, Marcelo was the kind of attacking left back every top-level club wanted.Bombing down the left flank for Los Blancos, the Brazilian was defensively sound in his prime while also providing goals, assists and attacking support. In the physical, counter attacking environment of English soccer, Marcelo could have been a perfect fit.

Thomas Müller. / IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters ConnectThomas Müller’s movement, creativity and finishing have made him one of the world’s most intelligent forwards in his prime. Manchester United pursued him in 2014, but he opted to stay in Germany with Bayern Munich, eventually leaving for a swan song in MLS during the twilight of his career.

Toni Kroos won it all with Real Madrid. / Justin Setterfield/Getty ImagesThe Premier League came tantalizingly close to welcoming Toni Kroos in 2014, when he was reportedly on the verge of joining Manchester United and bringing his midfield mastery to English soccer.But David Moyes’s dismissal and Louis van Gaal’s appointment changed the picture. The deal fell through, allowing Real Madrid to swoop in instead.

Could Yamal come to England one day? / David Ramos/Getty ImagesAlready a two-time Ballon d’Or runner-up and three-time Kopa Trophy winner, Lamine Yamal has practically his entire career ahead of him if he ever fancies a move to the Premier League.Any club would no doubt have to break the world transfer record to prize him away, though.

Figo was a baller. / Paolo Cocco/Getty ImagesCreatively relentless and blessed with the pace and power to match, Luís Figo could have been the perfect player to tear the Premier League apart at the height of his powers.Five years at Barcelona saw him blossom into arguably the world’s finest soccer player—and his controversial move to Real Madrid in 2000 did little to diminish his legacy.

Puyol was made for the Prem. / David Ramos/Getty ImagesAnother case where you have to admire the loyalty, but Carles Puyol was built for the Barclays era, in truth.A no-nonsense defender who loved nothing more than crunching into tackles, taking ankles and throwing himself in front of shots on the goal line. His combative style and natural leadership would have made him an even bigger cult hero in the Premier League.

Karim Benzema never made it to England. / USA TODAY SportsThere were faint hopes that, after his legendary spell at Real Madrid came to an end, Ballon d’Or winner Karim Benzema might make one final splash in the Premier League.Alas, the riches of the Saudi Pro League came calling, and it wasn’t to be.

Neuer was the ultimate sweeper-keeper. / Sebastian Widmann/Getty ImagesDominating the late 2000s and early 2010s with his reinvention and popularization of the sweeper-keeper role, Manuel Neuer has always been something of a loose cannon.His imposing physical presence and modernized style would have shocked English soccer, but perhaps only accelerated an evolution the game was already undergoing.

Rivaldo won the 1999 Ballon d'Or. / Phil Cole /Allsport/Getty ImagesGoals, assists, flair, vision and physicality—Rivaldo had just about everything you could want in a star forward. Better yet, he wasn’t restricted to a second-striker role.He won the Ballon d’Or in 1999 while playing for Barcelona, just as David Beckham was establishing himself as one of England’s most creative talents. Bringing the Brazilian to the Premier League would have set up a fascinating battle between two of the game’s most gifted playmakers.

What a sight Carlos would have been in the Prem. / Shaun Botterill/Getty ImagesThe Premier League has enjoyed some extraordinary free kick specialists over the years, but the division never had the pleasure of watching Roberto Carlos unleash one of his trademark rockets from long range.

Totti was always loyal to Roma. / Getty ImagesThe Premier League could use a few more Italian streaks of loyalty, and there is no one better suited to deliver them than Francesco Totti.A romantic departure from Roma to become a Barclays-era cult hero was always a long shot. But what a wonderful sight it would have been.
